note: Full text for the authored entries only. Use these as the voice for scenarios and feedback. For every other id, use your own knowledge. Do not invent a quotation.

entries.name: survivorship bias
entries.subtitle: where your mind tricks you
entries.law: the evidence that lived is loud; the evidence that died says nothing.
entries.notes: the planes that came home show you where armor isn't needed. the failures never report back. the sample you can see is not the sample that was.

entries.name: schelling point
entries.subtitle: how to win when others play too
entries.law: with no way to speak, people still find the same place to meet.
entries.notes: with no communication, people still converge on the same answer. the focal point each expects the other to expect. coordination without a word.

entries.name: goodhart's law
entries.subtitle: how things connect and ripple
entries.law: what happens when the measuring stick becomes the thing being measured.
entries.notes: when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure. push on any metric hard enough and the system starts producing the number itself instead of the outcome the number was meant to track.

entries.name: mimetic desire
entries.subtitle: why people do what they do
entries.law: we don't choose what we want. we catch it from each other.
entries.notes: we borrow our wants from models we admire. and when two people want through the same model, they want the same thing. rivalry follows.

entries.name: inversion
entries.subtitle: how to think clearly
entries.law: to master a problem, study how to fail at it, then refuse to.
entries.notes: instead of asking how to succeed, ask what would guarantee failure, then avoid it. many hard problems dissolve when worked backward.

entries.name: via negativa
entries.subtitle: how to decide and act
entries.law: the surest improvement is removing what's wrong, not adding what's clever.
entries.notes: improvement by subtraction: strip the fragile, the false, and the unnecessary before adding anything clever. what you remove can't break.

entries.name: gell-mann amnesia
entries.subtitle: how to know what's true
entries.law: you trust the report on every subject but the one you happen to know.
entries.notes: you read a story about a subject you know deeply and catch every error. you turn the page to a subject you don't know, and trust it completely.
